record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: small crowded Baire CDH sets of reals
record.original_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that there is a crowded countable dense homogeneous subset X of the real line whose cardinality is less than the continuum c and which is a Baire space?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Is there consistently a crowded CDH set X ⊆ R of size less than c which is Baire?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. A space is crowded (also called dense-in-itself) if it has no isolated points. A space is a Baire space if the intersection of any countable family of dense open sets is dense. Let $\mathfrak{c}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum.

Determine whether the following statement is consistent with ZFC: there exists a subset $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ (with the subspace topology inherited from the usual topology on $\mathbb{R}$) such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is crowded,
\item $X$ is countable dense homogeneous,
\item $X$ is a Baire space, and
\item $|X| < \mathfrak{c}$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on countable dense homogeneity (e.g., Hernández-Gutiérrez–Hrušák–van Mill and subsequent work through 2025) continues to list as open whether it is consistent that there is a crowded Baire CDH metric (or real) space of size less than the continuum. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and λ-sets
status_evidence.snippet: It is consistent that every CDH metric space has size ω1 or c; question whether a Baire CDH metric space of size less than c can exist remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The consistency of a Baire CDH crowded metric space of size less than c is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on CDH spaces, including Baire CDH groups, still references the size-vs-Baire question as unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues to investigate but does not resolve the consistency of small crowded Baire CDH sets.
